source_anchors.operation: FeatureMap owns an IdentificationData id_data_ member; this port attaches identification records by reference instead, so Clone and PartialEq survive
ConsensusMap owns the same IdentificationData member, with the same divergence

FeatureMap::operator== compares data_, MetaInfoInterface, RangeManagerType, DocumentIdentifier, UniqueIdInterface and the three record vectors; DocumentIdentifier::operator== itself compares only the identifier, so the loaded file path and type do not take part
operator+= resets ranges, document identifier and unique ID, concatenates the records, then resolves conflicting unique IDs through UniqueIdIndexer
FeatureMap::swap swaps features, ranges, document identifier, unique ID and index, records and id_data_, but NOT the inherited MetaInfoInterface; meta values stay with their map

getPrimaryMSRunPath assigns into the caller's list only when spectra_data exists and appends UNKNOWN only when the resulting list is empty, so a non-empty output argument is kept and the placeholder suppressed
clear(false) clears data_ only, leaving the cached ranges populated, which is why the source's operator== distinguishes a cleared map from a default one
appendRows zips the merged column-header map against rhs's header map positionally, renaming and summing sizes for the shorter prefix rather than matching by column index
appendRows sorts and deduplicates the fixed and variable modification lists of every protein identification in the merged map, including the pre-existing ones
appendColumns shifts rhs's column indices by the header COUNT of the left map, not by its largest index, so sparse keys can still collide and std::map::insert keeps the existing header
ConsensusMap::swap swaps every member except the inherited MetaInfoInterface, the same asymmetry as FeatureMap::swap
setPrimaryMSRunPath writes paths into column_description_[i] by position; std::map::operator[] default-inserts, so a map whose headers are keyed otherwise gains columns instead of being renamed
the path-count check applies only when column_description_ is non-empty, so an empty map silently accepts any number of paths
split sizes its result by column_description_.size() but indexes it with the map index, reading out of bounds when the headers are not keyed 0..n-1
the isobaric branch dereferences new_feats.begin() without checking that the consensus feature has any handle
new_feats[pep_id.getMetaValue("map_index")] default-inserts a BaseFeature, so an identification whose map index has no handle still creates a feature there
the isobaric branch copies every ProteinIdentification into the first feature map, which the source comment itself marks as wrong
BaseFeature(const FeatureHandle&) slices the handle to its Peak2D base, so split carries position, intensity, charge and width but not the handle's unique ID
updateUniqueIdToIndex throws Exception::Postcondition only when the number of DISTINCT valid IDs differs from the number of valid IDs, so a container of unassigned elements is accepted
resolveUniqueIdConflicts assigns an ID to every unassigned element without counting it, and loops without bound while the drawn ID is already taken
getPrimaryMSRunPath strips a file:/// prefix only to choose the path separator and then joins using the unstripped path
applyFunctionOnPeptideHits / applyFunctionOnPeptideIDs, inherited by both maps from a header outside this work package; plain Rust iteration over the public record vectors is the counterpart

evidence: Tier 3 (source review): every literal in tests/map_operations.rs is transcribed from the two pinned class tests; no C++ was built or executed, and no retained C++ output exists for these headers. Class-test section accounting: FeatureMap_test.cpp 32 sections, 32 ported, 0 mapped-with-evidence, 0 unaccounted; ConsensusMap_test.cpp 39 sections, 39 ported, 0 mapped-with-evidence, 0 unaccounted. The eight NOT_TESTABLE sections of ConsensusMap_test.cpp are ported as real tests rather than mapped. Two sections diverge from the transcribed expectation and say so at the assertion: the final case of FeatureMap_test.cpp operator==/operator!= and of ConsensusMap_test.cpp operator==/operator!= expects a map cleared with clear(false) to differ from a default map, because the source's operator== compares the RangeManager cache that clear(false) leaves populated; this port computes ranges on demand, has no such cache, and the two maps compare equal. Everything the port checks that the source does not - the container ceilings, the bounded unique-ID redraw, the checked map-index range in split, the atomic reference translation and the rejected non-integer map_index - is tier 4 (Rust-only invariants), derived from the anchored source lines above.
